title: study_note@v1
description: Reading note taken from ONE source: what it establishes, with the bibliographic data needed to cite it under the citation standard the brief names. One per source; assembled into collection<study_note@v1> by the map node.

source.description: Human-readable identifier of the source this note came from. Downstream stages reference notes by this value.

is_source.description: False for a working file that reached the collection but is not source material (a search log, a list of unreachable sites). Such a file must never appear in the report's reference list.
is_source.$comment: The engine keeps the finder's own _index.json and open-questions.md out of the collection, but a kept source file can still turn out to be a list of what could not be retrieved rather than material; a live run had one cited as a source.

source_kind.description: The nature of the document, chosen by what it IS rather than what it is about. A machine vocabulary: language-neutral tokens, whatever language the note's prose is in.

source_kind_detail.description: What the document is in the brief's own terms (statute, ruling, standard, benchmark, filing, vendor manual). Required in spirit when source_kind is `other`: the generic vocabulary is deliberately coarse, and this field is where the specificity lives.

primacy.description: How directly this source carries what it reports. Kept separate from trust_level because they answer different questions: a thorough news article restating an official figure is a restatement however reliable it is, and counting it as a second source would make a claim look twice as well founded as it is.

bibliography.description: Everything needed to build the reference entry. Leave a field out rather than inventing it.

entry.description: The source formatted as one reference entry per the citation standard the brief names, built ONLY from data the source states about itself.

container.description: Journal, collection, publisher or issuing body.

incomplete_fields.description: Bibliographic fields the source does not state, so downstream stages know the entry is partial rather than guessing at it.

key_points.description: What this source genuinely establishes. Empty is valid for a source that turned out to carry nothing.

text.description: One self-contained statement, in the report's language, of what the source establishes.

quote.description: Verbatim wording where the wording itself carries weight.

locator.description: Page, section, article, paragraph, table — whatever lets a reader verify the statement.

figures.description: Quantitative data, each with the period it covers. A figure without its period cannot be used in an argument about change over time.

period.description: The period the figure covers, as the source states it. Record the absence rather than inferring a period from context.

cited_refs.description: Identifiers this source names, as it names them: norms, case numbers, standards, datasets, prior work, registration numbers.

aspect_ids.description: Which of the brief's required aspects this note can support, by the brief's own numbering. What makes coverage checkable instead of a matter of opinion.

open_questions.description: Gaps, contradictions or ambiguities in this source. Prefer flagging over smoothing over.

trust_level.description: How much weight the source carries, given its authority and completeness. Orthogonal to primacy.
